speaker: Doctor
text:
I see you have a complex history; to understand the progression of your gait and limb ataxia, have you noticed any recent changes in your memory, personality, or coordination?

REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with focus on cerebellum and brainstem
REQUEST TEST: Genetic_panel_for_ataxia

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Multiple sclerosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is a critical piece of information; natalizumab is a known risk factor for Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML), which can present with ataxia. Have you noticed any vision changes, weakness in your limbs, or speech difficulties recently?

REQUEST TEST: JC_virus_serology
REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain full sequence with focus on white matter lesions

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: JC_virus_serology: JC virus antibody positive (seroconversion consistent with active infection). MRI Brain full sequence with focus on white matter lesions: T1/T2 images showing multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement, indicative of Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML).

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy.

You must stop taking natalizumab immediately to halt the progression of this opportunistic infection caused by the JC virus. We will need to consult neurology and infectious disease specialists to discuss treatment options such as stopping the drug and potentially initiating immune reconstitution therapies.
